stackAndServices: TypeScript/NestJS monorepo. apps/api (NestJS API), apps/worker (BullMQ job consumers), apps/dashboard (React web UI). libs/application-generic (ChatFactory/ChatWebhookHandler wiring), packages/providers (ChatWebhookProvider — axios POST + HMAC-SHA256 signing), packages/shared (provider enum/config), packages/framework (bridge schema). Store: MongoDB (subscribers, integrations, notification execution logs) + Redis/BullMQ (trigger job queue). Egress: outbound HTTP POST from worker to a subscriber-configured webhookUrl, signed via X-Novu-Signature HMAC header.
conjureFeasibility: Mostly REAL. The egress leg is genuinely conjurable as a WALK, not a stub: Chat Webhook is a generic, non-vendor-specific provider — the "destination" is whatever URL the subscriber's credentials record, so a harness-run, harness-controlled HTTP receiver satisfies P'(b)'s "user-configured destination aimed at a controlled receiver" carve-out with no fixed-vendor CND forced. The API/worker/dashboard/Mongo/Redis stack is directly conjurable from the repo's own docker-compose/dev topology — no doubling needed there either. The one non-REAL element is the precondition itself: setting the subscriber's webhookUrl credential is, per Novu's own docs, only exposed via the Subscribers API/SDK, never through dashboard UI — so under a strict click/type/navigate-only front door, that precondition cannot be built at all, which is a constructability gap rather than a fixture/vendor problem. No third-party essence, no sealed-out effect — this PR was a good pick for stressing the egress check without also forcing CND on vendor grounds.
verdictBasis: The discriminating claim requires a subscriber whose chat credentials include a webhookUrl pointing at a harness-controlled receiver. Per Novu's own subscriber docs, that credential is settable only through the Subscribers API/SDK — there is no dashboard click/type/navigate path to set it. A driver held strictly to P'(a)'s "only click/type/navigate/read — no request forging, no deep links" therefore cannot construct the walk's precondition at all: the setup step is NOT-EXECUTABLE via the front door as defined, which per (c) forces NOT-EXECUTED -> CND for the pre-registered claim, independent of whether the underlying delivery mechanism works. Confession: if "front door" is read more loosely to include the product's own documented, authenticated API/SDK calls (which, for an API-first infra product like Novu, is arguably the primary way a real integrating "user" acts), then my read of the diff predicts the mainline case WORKS — the ChatWebhookProvider is a near-verbatim reuse of the pre-existing PushWebhookPushProvider's createBody/computeHmac/axios-post pattern, wired through the same ChatFactory/BaseChatHandler machinery already exercising traffic for Slack/Discord/Teams — so the core "signed POST arrives, content-bound to the trigger" behavior is plausible-WORKS. notCovered: I did not and could not run the actual harness (no live Novu instance, no receiver, no dashboard session in this pass) — this is a diff+docs-grounded prediction only, and I did not verify whether the dashboard's Activity Feed exposes per-message delivery detail sufficient for a persisted-state corroborating leg.
holds: P'(b)'s egress carve-out fires cleanly here: because Chat Webhook targets an arbitrary user-configured URL rather than a fixed vendor, a harness-owned receiver is a legitimate controlled-receiver WALK, not a stub — avoiding the fixed-vendor CND that Slack/Discord/Teams providers would have forced.

Content-binding substitutes for the fresh-session leg exactly as the theory intends: the HMAC-SHA256 signature is computed over the exact serialized body (content/webhookUrl/channel/phoneNumber), so the harness can cryptographically tie one outbound POST to one specific trigger rather than accepting 'some POST arrived'.

The sealed-room 'BLOCKS+records undeclared egress' mechanism maps onto a real code path in this diff, not a hypothetical: bridgeProviderData can override data.body.webhookUrl at send time, and an allowlisted sealed room would correctly catch/flag an attempt to redirect egress off the subscriber's configured host.

Hostile classes (wrong subscriber, missing secret, filtered step) each correspond to a concrete branch visible in the diff (the falsy-secretKey early return in computeHmac, the per-subscriber webhookUrl lookup), so the hostile-class menu is groundable in real code, not generic boilerplate.

breaks.detail: The subscriber webhookUrl credential — the precondition the whole discriminating claim depends on — is API/SDK-only in current Novu; there is no dashboard UI path to set it. A driver following P'(a) literally (clicks/typing/navigation only) cannot build the walk's setup state at all.
breaks.fix: Define an explicit front-door rule for API-first products: authenticated calls to the product's own documented, versioned public API/SDK count as user-shaped actions equivalent to UI clicks (this is the developer's actual 'front door'), while ad hoc curl against undocumented/internal endpoints, direct DB writes, or feature-flag bypasses remain forbidden request-forging.

breaks.detail: bridgeProviderData lets the sending code override the destination URL (data.body.webhookUrl) independent of the subscriber's stored credential. If the sealed room's allowlist is scoped by subscriber/workflow identity rather than by the specific expected destination host, a substitution (same subscriber, swapped receiver host) could slip past the effect check as a false WORKS.
breaks.fix: Bind the egress effect check to (destination host == subscriber's currently configured webhookUrl credential) AND (signature verifies against configured secret) — not just 'a POST landed in the sealed room for this subscriber.'

breaks.detail: The credential schema marks hmacSecretKey required:false, but computeHmac returns undefined when no secret is set, producing header 'X-Novu-Signature': undefined rather than omitting signing or failing loudly. A schema-legal, non-adversarial configuration (no secret) breaks the 'signature is verifiable' claim in the mainline path, not just under hostile input.
breaks.fix: Either make the secret required in the schema, or have sendMessage skip the signature header entirely (and record that fact) when unset, so 'signature verifiable' becomes a pre-registerable, checkable claim rather than a silently-degraded default.

breaks.detail: I could not confirm whether Novu's Activity Feed exposes per-message delivery-attempt detail (vs. channel-level status only) to serve as the persisted-state corroborating leg for non-egress claims tied to this feature.
breaks.fix: Before running the harness, spot-check the Activity Feed/execution-detail API response shape for a chat step to confirm it carries a distinct identifier the effect check can bind to.

sonnetDifficulty: Two things were genuinely hard for me, a Sonnet-level agent, not just tedious. First, WebSearch results were unreliable noise for PR discovery — it surfaced tangential/wrong PRs (#2074, #5139) as 'webhook' matches; I had to abandon it and fall back to `gh search prs --repo novuhq/novu ... --merged --json ...`, which was far more precise. A less careful pass could easily have picked a wrong or non-existent PR off WebSearch's confident-sounding summary. Second, the front-door-constructability problem (dashboard can't set subscriber credentials) was not visible from the diff at all — I initially assumed the dashboard probably had a subscriber-credentials editor and only caught the gap by deliberately WebFetching the subscriber docs and reading the explicit 'API/SDK only' language. Third, spotting the SSRF-shaped override vector (data.body.webhookUrl) required close, line-by-line reading of a 20-line function plus cross-referencing a completely separate, later PR (#11378, SSRF protection for email/SMS webhook providers) to notice its fix did NOT extend to this chat-webhook path — that 'they patched siblings but not this one' inference is a diff-differencing move I would not reliably make under time pressure, and it's exactly the kind of thing a genius-tier reviewer catches on reflex and a rushed Sonnet pass skips. Deciding whether 'dashboard can't set credentials' should resolve to CND (strict reading) or WORKS (API-as-front-door reading) was a judgment call with no clean mechanical resolution in the theory as written — that ambiguity itself is a risk, since different runs of me could resolve it inconsistently.
newVectors: FW-15 (proposed) 'API-native front door': for API-first/infra products, the real user-shaped action for many setup/trigger flows has no UI path at all (only a documented public API/SDK call). A strictly UI-only front-door reading systematically produces false-CND (not false-WORKS) on this class of product, which is a coverage failure mode the known list (FW-1/2/3/11/12/14) doesn't name — it inverts the usual failure direction (too conservative instead of too permissive).

CND-boundary: 'override-at-send-time' fields in a generic egress payload (bridgeProviderData) let developer-controlled code redirect the destination independent of the stored credential the setup step configured. The sealed room must allowlist per-claim by the credential-derived destination host, not merely by subscriber/workflow identity, or a same-actor/different-host substitution evades the egress effect check.
openQuestions: Does the dashboard's Activity Feed / execution detail expose per-message delivery-attempt granularity (provider response, timestamp, distinct message id) usable as a persisted-state corroborating leg, or only channel-level status?

Is there a genuine 'Test Workflow' trigger button in the current dashboard that pushes a real job through the worker's BullMQ queue end-to-end (exercising the actual ChatWebhookHandler/provider path), or does dashboard test-trigger take a shortcut that bypasses the worker?

Does BaseProvider.transform's CamelCase casing step silently rename/rewrite the webhookUrl or hmacSecretKey override keys in bridgeProviderData in a way that changes the override behavior analyzed from the diff alone?
compiledPromise: Discriminating claim: for a workflow trigger fired through Novu's front door (dashboard test-trigger or the developer's registered API-key-authenticated trigger call) against a Chat step configured with a 'Chat Webhook' integration (HMAC secret set) and a subscriber whose chat credentials.webhookUrl points at a harness-controlled receiver, exactly one HTTP POST arrives at that receiver within the action window whose JSON body's rendered content matches this specific trigger's payload and whose X-Novu-Signature header verifies as HMAC-SHA256(body, configured secret) against the same-window notification/execution record Novu persists for that trigger (content-binding substitutes for the fresh-session leg, per the EGRESS clause). Negative: for (i) a different/unrelated subscriber, (ii) a step-condition-filtered subscriber, or (iii) a trigger with no matching Chat Webhook integration configured, no POST arrives at that receiver in the window, and the persisted execution record reflects skip/failure rather than a false 'delivered'. Quantifier check (FW-11): run against >=2 distinct subscriber+webhookUrl pairs not held by the configuring actor, plus >=1 out-of-scope subscriber as negative, before accepting any 'works for subscribers generally' framing.
